trust_decision.summary: File-declared geometry (width/height/channels) decides allocation size; the library allocates a full black-fill buffer for a failed channel decode regardless of how few input bytes back it (decompress), and the canvas guard ignores channel count (check_pixel_size).

landing_point.why: Summary names composite/numpy and geometry; the numpy entry already calls check_pixel_size, so an engineer looks there and at utils.check_pixel_size first, not at the codec's black-fill fallback.

fix_sites.entry_point: PSDImage.numpy()/topil()/composite() and Layer.numpy()/topil(), plus public psd_tools.compression.decompress()

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report says composite/numpy and the canvas guard already exists there, so a solver can argue the codec's lenient black-fill fallback is intended graceful-degradation behaviour (documented via PSDDecompressionWarning) and leave it alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Small or legitimately sized corrupt channels must still warn and be black-filled instead of raising; within-spec canvases must not be rejected by default (byte budget is opt-in, default None).
